timestamp_semantics: monotonic logical append time after Campaign198 terminal authority, complete skill read and bounded Campaign199 repository checks
purpose: Freeze a finite enterprise service and technical-support entitlement, request intake, ticket backlog, response, resolution, escalation, reopening, SLA and corrective-action lifecycle before source rows, case values, formulas, directions, comparators, security prices or returns.

repository_evidence.bounded_search_scope: Existing Campaign160 and Campaign166-198 source-frontier metadata only
repository_evidence.campaign160_boundary: The no-credential inventory admits no complete point-in-time service-desk, technical-support or field-service case history. Selling expense, warranty provision, contract liability or service revenue cannot substitute for case states.
repository_evidence.campaign166_boundary: Campaign166 freezes recalls, production interruptions, safety events, cybersecurity incidents and service outages. An incident is an operating shock; it does not identify entitlement, intake, assignment, backlog, response, resolution, escalation, reopening or SLA clocks across all support cases.
repository_evidence.campaign168_boundary: Campaign168 freezes customer, user and installed-footprint scale. An installed base or active-user count may be a denominator, but it does not identify support entitlement, case arrivals, backlog stock flow or case-state transitions.
repository_evidence.campaign169_boundary: Campaign169 freezes prices, fees, discounts and commercial terms. A maintenance fee, service credit or support-tier price does not establish whether a case was entitled, assigned, responded to, resolved, reopened or escalated.
repository_evidence.campaign170_boundary: Campaign170 already freezes complaints, service resolution, satisfaction, returns, warranty and retention outcomes. Campaign199 is limited to case-operating process states across entitled service requests; complaint counts, satisfaction or resolution rates cannot be relabelled as a new factor.
repository_evidence.campaign183_boundary: Campaign183 freezes IP and software-license rights plus support and maintenance obligations. A contractual support right does not establish the realized case queue, response clock, resolution state, escalation, root cause or recurrence history.
repository_evidence.sector_scope_boundary: Applicable issuers, service products, contract support, field service, technical support and outsourced service desks must be frozen. Structurally inapplicable issuers may not be filled with zero or cross-sector ranked.
repository_evidence.point_in_time_boundary: A current service dashboard, ticket export or SLA scorecard cannot be projected backward without case creation, status transition, reassignment, escalation, reopening, correction, deletion and first-public histories.

finite_prevalue_catalog.name: complaint_satisfaction_refund_warranty_repair_retention_or_resolution_kpi_relabeling
finite_prevalue_catalog.economic_state: A complaint count, satisfaction score, refund, warranty claim, repair, retention, churn or published resolution-rate KPI relabelled as support-case operating lifecycle quality.
finite_prevalue_catalog.reason: Campaign170 already governs complaint, satisfaction, return, warranty, service-resolution and retention outcomes. Those outcomes do not create a separate case-state stock flow, entitlement or clock history.

finite_prevalue_catalog.reason: Campaign166 already freezes incident families. Incident progress or resolution cannot substitute for the complete entitled support-case population and ordinary case-state transitions.

finite_prevalue_catalog.name: support_contract_license_maintenance_fee_service_credit_customer_user_or_installed_base_relabeling
finite_prevalue_catalog.economic_state: A support contract, software license, maintenance price, service credit amount, customer count, user count or installed base relabelled as realized support operations.
finite_prevalue_catalog.reason: Scale, pricing and contractual rights are already frozen domains. They do not identify case arrival, backlog, assignment, response, resolution, escalation, reopening or corrective-action transitions.

finite_prevalue_catalog.name: service_product_channel_customer_priority_severity_tier_direction_threshold_age_window_subset_combination_or_model_variant
finite_prevalue_catalog.economic_state: A selected service, product, channel, customer, priority, severity, support tier, direction, threshold, case age, business-hours window, subset, normalization, interaction, combined score or fitted model from unadmitted case histories.
